analysis.title: Up and Adam
key_insights: The S&P 500 rose 1.6% on 11/4/2026, the first post-midterm session. It was the second-strongest post-midterm rally since 1982, behind only 2018. The index has risen 72% of the time in the first post-midterm session since 1930.
Consumer Discretionary and Financials led the rally. Energy pulled back alongside lower oil prices.

The four largest hyperscalers gained an average of 4.4% despite the risk of stricter data center rules from new governors in key states. Raymond James reasons that slower new builds would shift the AI bottleneck from chip supply to access to existing computing capacity, which hyperscalers dominate. Less capex and capital raising could also ease pressure on their balance sheets.

WTI crude fell another 8% and closed at its lowest level since August 31, after already declining on signs of improving US-Iran dialogue. The move followed VP Vance's post: "The reason we lost is the war." Markets read it as a more dovish stance toward Iran. Raymond James cautions that no durable settlement has been reached.

Raymond James sees room for legislative compromise under divided government on a narrow set of issues: energy permitting, higher defense spending and possibly health insurance subsidies. Democrats may push provisions limiting data centers. The White House's $1.5t FY27 budget request is unlikely to pass.

ADP private employment rose 86k in October, above expectations and matching September's downwardly revised gain. Hiring was broad across firm sizes, led by services, with construction helped by the data center buildout. Combined with a stronger than expected JOLTS report, Raymond James views the labor market as broadly healthy.
Raymond James expects Friday's nonfarm payrolls at +70k, with the unemployment rate holding at 4.2%.
